query: door-to-needle time thrombolysis process mapping improvement primary stroke centre
sourcesConsulted: model knowledge of stroke pathway improvement reports
gradeRationale: Certainty is left to the appraisal of the retrieved records.
synthesis: Four further reports are suggested as leads alongside the six retrieved records: mobile stroke units, nurse-initiated stroke protocols in regional emergency departments, single-bolus thrombolytics and telestroke in rural hospitals. None has been retrieved or checked; they are leads to search for, not evidence.

items.title: Mobile stroke units versus standard ambulance response: time to thrombolysis
items.keyFindings: Treatment in the ambulance shortened time from alarm to thrombolysis by about 30 minutes in urban settings.
items.limitations: Urban services; costly; not an option for this hospital.

items.title: Nurse-initiated stroke protocols in regional emergency departments
items.keyFindings: Emergency nurses ordering CT and bloods on pre-alert shortened arrival-to-CT times in three regional hospitals.
items.notes: Lead; the year came back as text.

items.title: Single-bolus thrombolytic and door-to-needle time: a single-centre comparison
items.keyFindings: A bolus-only drug removed the infusion set-up step and shortened needle times by a few minutes.
items.limitations: One centre; drug change coincided with other changes.
items.notes: Lead; formulary decisions are outside the project.

items.title: Telestroke consultation and thrombolysis times in rural hospitals: a systematic review
items.authors: Oyelowo-Brandt S, Quist-Morales P, Fischer-Obi N
items.keyFindings: Telestroke gave door-to-needle times similar to on-site assessment in most included studies.
items.notes: Lead; relevant to the out-of-hours registrar problem.

summary: Four leads suggested; certainty left to the appraisal of retrieved records.
